 29s ago 15.05 EDT 4 min: There was a bit of early intent from Milan but overall, a steady start for both teams. But wait! A chance for Kluivert from close range, who misses his kick, then Gannon-Doak has a shot blocked! That could easily have been 1-0. The fans are in fine voice.
 Share Updated at  15.05 EDT 2m ago 15.03 EDT 3 min: There were four changes for Bournemouth, by the way, with Ben Gannon-Doak, Bafode Diakite, Justin Kluivert and Michele Di Gregorio (in goal) coming into the side.
 Share 4m ago 15.01 EDT First half kick-off!
 The football has begun, at a rain-lashed Vitality Stadium on the south coast.
 Share 5m ago 15.01 EDT Celtic v Celta Vigo teams
 Celtic : Johnstone, Donovan, Murray, Scales, Tierney, McGregor, Baur, Hassan, Nygren, Osmand, Duran. Substitutes : Sinisalo, Lotomba, Hogh, McCowan, Tounekti, Sorensen, Oxlade-Chamberlain, Forrest, Ralston, Kennedy, Haney, McArdle.
 Celta Vigo: Radu, Rodriguez, Caceres, Alonso, Rueda, Burcio, Febas, Carreira, Aspas, Jutgla, Alvarez. Substitutes : Bayindir, Faye, Moriba, Duran, Gonzalez, Lago, Swedberg, Galan, Driouech, Antanon, Arcos, Milla.
 Referee: Georgi Kabakov (Bulgaria)
 Share 6m ago 14.59 EDT Bournemouth’s Marco Rose on TNT Sports a little while ago: “We need to control the load … I have to take care about the lads, and that’s why some changes.”
 Share 7m ago 14.59 EDT Besiktas v Crystal Palace teams
 It’s Danny “unfeasibly neat hair” Makkelie on the whistle!
 Besiktas: Nubel, Bulut, Djalo, Akdag, Ouattara, Ndidi, Trossard, Miretti, Kartal Yilmaz, Fakili, Oh. Substitutes : Alemdar, Salih Ozcan, Agbadou, Olaitan, Poku, Cerny, Vlahovic, Ridvan Yilmaz, Topcu, Yasin Ozcan, Murillo, Kilicsoy.
 Crystal Palace: Benitez, Richards, Disasi, Canvot, Khalaili, Wharton, Kamada, Mitchell, McNeil, Pino, Mateta. Substitutes : Matthews, Benetton, Sarr, Nketiah, Hughes, Ahanor, Larsen, Osorio, Mingueza, Chilwell, Benamar, King.
 Referee: Danny Makkelie (Holland)
 Share 8m ago 14.57 EDT Thanks Daniel. The latest furore at perma-crisis club Manchester United begs the question: was Ruben Amorim really that bad?
 Entirely unfairly, we can consider Bournemouth v Milan as a referendum on his managerial ability. Here we go!
 Share 10m ago 14.55 EDT Bournemouth v Milan teams
 Bournemouth: Di Gregorio, Diakite, Hill, Silva, Truffert, Tavernier, Christie, Adams, Doak, Evanilson, Kluivert. Substitutes : Petrovic, Allan, Cook, Soler, Brooks, Smith, Adli, Toth, Rodriguez, Rayan.
 Milan: Maignan, Tomori, De Winter, Pavlovic, Hutchinson, Musah, Jashari, Estupinan, Loftus-Cheek, Moreira, Cisse. Substitutes : Bouyer, Torriani, Pulisic, Rabiot, Diawara, Modric, Comotto, Bartesaghi, Gila, Vladimirov, Camarda.
 Referee: Vassilis Fotias (Greece)
 Share 12m ago 14.54 EDT Righto, my watch is over for now. I’ll be back shortly but, in the meantime, here’s Luke McLaughlin to coax you through the imminent first halves.
 Share 13m ago 14.53 EDT Looking ahead to the later round of games, Palace have to find a way of bouncing back following their tousing at Brighton. Pierre Sage doesn’t look to have settled at the club yet, and could really use a result tonight to right things.
 Share 17m ago 14.49 EDT Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal Read more Share 18m ago 14.48 EDT Next in line? Main contenders for the Manchester United hot seat Read more Share 20m ago 14.46 EDT Conference League final scores
 Photograph: The Guardian Share 21m ago 14.45 EDT Europa League final scores
 Photograph: The Guardian Share 23m ago 14.43 EDT FULL TIME: Trabzonspor 2-0 Heart of Midlothian
 Hearts were much better than at Celtic, but they still lose.
 Share 23m ago 14.42 EDT RED CARD! Trabzonspor's Lopes Cabral is sent off for a second yellow card
 90+5 min It’s harsh, a pull-back out wide, but what on earth is he doing not just letting Kerjota go. Now he misses a crucial game against Freiburg.
 Share 25m ago 14.40 EDT And here it is. 
 Allow Instagram content? This article includes content provided by Instagram . We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue' .
 Allow and continue Share 26m ago 14.40 EDT Hearts haven’t quite finished losing to Trabzonspor. They’ll be naused about the penalty they didn’t get just before half-time, but the better side are in front and Franculino’s second goal was a banger.
 Share 27m ago 14.38 EDT FULL TIME: Jablonec 0-0 Brighton & Hove Albion
 Brighton have four points from two games and actually might well have lost tonight, so can have no complaints.
 Share 29m ago 14.37 EDT That Roefs double-save. Just look at it!
 Allow Instagram content? This article includes content provided by Instagram . We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue' .
 Allow and continue Share Updated at  14.37 EDT 30m ago 14.36 EDT FULL TIME: Lech Poznan 1-1 Sunderland
 Sunderland should’ve won, might’ve lost, and with seven points and two home games to come, they’re nicely set.
 Share 30m ago 14.35 EDT Then Brighton go up the other end and Rutter shoots … and Hanus saves.
 Share 31m ago 14.34 EDT The keeper punches it clear, and might that be Sunderland’s final opportunity? Brighton, meantime, almost lose it in Jablonec, Nebyla bending low and just around the post.
 Share 33m ago 14.32 EDT Into the final minute in Poznan, O’Nien’s throw earning a corner which yields another; we’re playing the first of three added minutes.
 Share 34m ago 14.31 EDT “Fabian Hürzeler may be a new kind of manager, but his lack of top level experience isn’t unheard of, writes Kári Tulinius. “Compared to Arrigo Sacchi, Hürzeler is James Milner. When criticised for his lack of playing experience, Sacchi famously quipped: ‘I never realised that to become a jockey you needed to be a horse first.’”
 Agree, it’s not unheard of, and the riposte is, of course, a classic, but it was unusual then whereas now, I think it’s likely to become a trend.
 Share 36m ago 14.30 EDT We’ve played 86 minutes in Poznan. If Sunderland have to make do with a draw, they’ll be disappointed because they’ve had enough chances to win several games but, on the other hand seven points from three games is pretty good and would put them well on the way to the top 24 if not the top eight.
 Share 39m ago 14.26 EDT Now Methalie attacks the Poznan box, weaving in from the left, shooting … just wide of the near post.
 Share 41m ago 14.25 EDT Le Fee’s been lively in the second half and he again sashays into the box and looks ready to shoot. But when the gap closes, he lays back for Rigg with lovely pace on the ball, used to send a left-footed curler inches over the angle – so close to goal it lands on the netting.
 Share 42m ago 14.23 EDT In Turin, Juventus have, my score has belatedly updated to tell me, equalised for 2-2 Rennes thanks to Woltemade’s penalty.
 Share 43m ago 14.22 EDT Jablonec are pushing, Verbruggen forces to beat away at his near post after Tchanturishvili carries down the left and shoots hard. Brighton have sent on Andres, David, Ayari and Boskovic for Gross, Boscagli, Hinshelwood and O’Riley.
 Share 48m ago 14.18 EDT Sunderland go in search of a winner, Le Fee opting not to shoot when he has an open lane, instead belatedly feeding Fofana, who slices wide of the near post.
 Share 49m ago 14.17 EDT Back in Jablonec, the home side have missed two chances, one a good one and the other a shot from distance.
 Share 49m ago 14.16 EDT AMAZING DOUBLE-SAVE FROM ROEFS!
 Ishak crosses from the left directly into the path of Walemark, who arrives on to it and punches hard from maybe seven yards. Roefs flings himself in the road, then Gurgul leathers the rebound from five yards, and somehow he’s up to dive in the way of that one too. That is so, so, so good, and Sunderland will lose this if they’re not careful.
 View image in fullscreen Michal Gurgul’s close range shot is saved by Sunderland keeper Robin Roefs, the second of an fantastic double save. Photograph: Tomasz Jedrzejowski/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Lech Poznan’s Patrik Walemark can’t believe that he, and Michal Gurgul, were denied by Robin Roefs reactions. Photograph: Paweł Jaskółka/PressFocus/MB Media/Getty Images Share Updated at  14.45 EDT 52m ago 14.14 EDT GOAL! Lech Poznan 1-1 Sunderland (Bengtsson 70)
 Ultimately, Sunsderland deserve this as punishment for the chances they’ve missed. A corner goes to the back post where Skrzypczak heads into O’Nien’s face. The ball drops to Bengtsson on the left side of the box, and he drills a competent low volley inside the near post.
 View image in fullscreen Lech Poznan’s Leo Bengtsson (left) celebrates scoring their equaliser with Mikael Ishak. Photograph: Kacper Pempel/Reuters View image in fullscreen Lech Poznan fans in the stands cheer their team on to hopefully add a second goal, now parity has been restored. Photograph: Kacper Pempel/Reuters Share Updated at  14.26 EDT 55m ago 14.11 EDT Le Fee wriggles space inside the Poznan box, trying a chapeau before fighting to regain possession, dragging a shot straight at the keeper. As time elapses, Sunderland need to keep going forward and resist temptation to sit on their lead, because Poznan look better equipped to score than avoid conceding.
 Share 1h ago 14.07 EDT OH WHAT A GOAL! Trabzonspor 2-0 Hearts (Franculino 58)
 He takes the ball out on the right and sways away from his marker, then megs Mato with a pass into Salah, who cleverly adjusts feet to guide a return into his path. Even so, there’s plenty to do, the ball under his feet but, from 15 yards, he digs out a curler into the far side-netting. That’s delicious behaviour.
 View image in fullscreen Franculino Dju (centre) celebrates scoring Trabzonspor’s second goal against Hearts. Photograph: Burak Kara/Uefa/Getty Images Share Updated at  14.13 EDT 1h ago 14.04 EDT Sunderland remove Mukiele, Angulo and Xhaka, with Rigg, Hume and Sadiki coming on.
 Share 1h ago 14.02 EDT Gosh, Sunderland might rue their profligacy. This time, Angulo, who’s had a really strong game, burrows to the by-line, cuts back, and Mukiele is there, inside the box with loads of time and space. He should place his shot, but instead lashes at it, and Lis tips behind for a corner. Xhaka swings it in, Ahoka ducks into a header … and Lis hurls himself right to tip away.
 Share 1h ago 13.59 EDT A ball flighted into Ishak … and this time, Danso does really well, craning his neck towards his own goal and around a clearing header. I think Sunderland will score again, as I said earlier, but they need to keep the back door shut. Oh, and here’s Angulo, taking a pass from Fofana that the defenders should cut out but don’t. He works a shooting lane, but doesn’t get hold of the effort, stubbing straight at the keeper.
 Share 1h ago 13.57 EDT More from Poznan… 
 View image in fullscreen 03de946f-1b6f-4687-83f5-c34f5 Photograph: Teacher, J Share 1h ago 13.56 EDT Nice from Sunderland, Mukiele cutting back from the by-line, perhaps just a little behind Diarra, who fetches it from around his arse and drills wide. That ought to have been 2-0.
 Share 1h ago 13.54 EDT Nice from Walemark, who twists O’Nien’s legs around each other, dips outside, shoot low … and the effort skips just by the far post.
 Share 1h ago 13.52 EDT We go again in Trabzonspor v Hearts.
 Share 1h ago 13.51 EDT Yalcouye slots home calmly for Brighton, but was at least 63 yards offside.
 Share 1h ago 13.51 EDT From the Poznan away end. 
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Pearlman, J Share Updated at  13.51 EDT 1h ago 13.48 EDT Off we go again in Jablonec and off we go again in Poznan.
 Share 1h ago 13.48 EDT I have a slightly different take on this: United have finally broken Bruno, jiggering his career with a series of poor decisions and broken promises. Of course, he’s responsible for his own behaviour, but the man is mad as hell and he’s not going to take this any more. Imagine United in the years since he signed without him.
 Share 1h ago 13.45 EDT Half-time reading: 
 Bruno’s betrayal? ‘Toxic’ Fernandes is symptom of United’s culture of entitlement | Jamie Jackson Read more Share 1h ago 13.39 EDT Conference League half-times
 Photograph: The Guardian Share 1h ago 13.38 EDT Europa League half-times
 Photograph: The Guardian Share 1h ago 13.37 EDT HALF-TIME: Trabzonspor 1-0 Hearts
 Salah’s penalty is the difference but Heart, having been gubbed 7-1 by Celtic at the weekend, are in this game.
 Share 2h ago 13.35 EDT HALF-TIME: Lech Poznan 0-1 Sunderland
 An entertaining first half, both sides looking to attack and Sunderland doing it better.
 Share 2h ago 13.34 EDT In Turkey, Claudio Braga attacks the by-line, Cabral slides in, doesn’t get the ball … and the ref say no penalty. I’d very much like to see his working.
